query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy is a solid refrigeration working medium that exhibits a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor load-bearing integrity and tends to crack. What single intervention could increase its integrity while preserving caloric performance in these operating regimes? State one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, predicted integrity and caloric outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, applicable field, pressure, temperature, and loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit results that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing 1–2 atomic percent Nb into the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy will form nanoscale coherent Nb-rich precipitates that enhance load-bearing integrity (fracture toughness and crack resistance) while preserving the caloric response under applied magnetic fields and moderate pressures.
generation.material_initial_state: (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy with intrinsic caloric phase transformations but poor load-bearing integrity due to cracking.
generation.intervention: Substitutional microalloying with ~1–2 at.% Nb added via arc melting.
generation.conditions: Arc melting to combine the constituents, followed by homogenization at approximately 1200°C for 1 hour and an aging treatment at about 600°C for 4 hours to promote controlled precipitation of Nb-rich coherent particles.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of nanoscale coherent Nb-rich precipitates localized at grain boundaries and within the grains.
generation.mechanism: The Nb-rich precipitates act as effective obstacles to crack initiation and propagation (dispersion strengthening and crack deflection) without significantly interfering with the martensitic phase transition mechanism that drives the caloric effect.
generation.predicted_outcome: Enhanced mechanical integrity (i.e., improved fracture toughness and resistance to cracking) with caloric performance preserved within the operating regimes (temperature window around 250–350 K; magnetic fields up to several Tesla; pressures up to a few hundred MPa).
generation.baseline: The unmodified (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy exhibits strong caloric responses under field and pressure but suffers from poor load-bearing properties leading to cracking.
generation.boundary: Operating conditions include field-induced transformations under moderate magnetic fields (up to several Tesla), applied pressures up to a few hundred MPa, and temperature range of approximately 250–350 K.
generation.uncertainty: It remains uncertain if the Nb addition will fully preserve the phase transformation kinetics of the martensitic transition; optimization of Nb concentration and aging parameters may be needed to prevent any adverse effects on the caloric performance.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy samples: one set with the standard composition and one with 1–2 at.% Nb added. Process both sets identically with arc melting, homogenization at 1200°C for 1 hour, and aging at 600°C for 4 hours. Conduct mechanical testing (fracture toughness, bending, or tensile tests) and caloric performance measurements (caloric effect under applied magnetic field and pressure) over the defined temperature and loading ranges.
measurements: Mechanical strength parameters (yield strength, ultimate tensile strength)
Magnitude of the caloric effect (e.g., isothermal entropy change, adiabatic temperature change)
Phase transition temperature range via differential scanning calorimetry (DSC)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Nb-added samples do not show a statistically significant improvement in fracture toughness (or equivalent load-bearing properties) compared to the baseline alloy, or if the caloric effect (magnitude or operational temperature range) is significantly deteriorated relative to the unmodified alloy, then the hypothesis would be falsified.

proposals.conditions: Prepare the alloy by arc melting followed by homogenization at ≈1200°C for 1 hour and an aging treatment at ≈600°C for 4 hours to promote the precipitation of Nb-rich, coherent particles
proposals.structural_mediator: Formation of nanoscale coherent Nb-rich precipitates localized at grain boundaries and within the grains

proposals.intervention: Thermomechanical processing via severe plastic deformation (SPD) coupled with subcritical annealing
proposals.conditions: Subject ingots to high-pressure torsion (HPT) or equal channel angular pressing (ECAP) at room temperature to induce substantial plastic strain followed by annealing at ≈500–550°C for 1–2 hours to stabilize a nanograined microstructure
proposals.structural_mediator: Nanograin formation with a bimodal grain size distribution; refined grains with engineered high-angle boundaries
proposals.mechanism: Grain refinement strengthens the alloy through the Hall–Petch mechanism and minimizes stress concentrations at coarse grain boundaries, thereby enhancing resistance to crack propagation while preserving the transformation characteristics that enable the caloric response
proposals.predicted_outcome: Improved load-bearing integrity through enhanced yield strength and toughness, while the caloric phase transformation (activated under similar magnetic field and pressure conditions) remains as active as in the baseline alloy
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: By modifying the microstructure without altering the chemical composition, the approach reinforces mechanical properties directly while maintaining the phase transformation responsible for the caloric response

proposals.intervention: In situ formation of a ductile secondary phase via minor Cu addition
proposals.conditions: Incorporate approximately 1–2 wt.% Cu during melting (e.g., arc melting) to promote liquid‐phase sintering followed by controlled cooling and a brief homogenization at ≈1100°C for 30 minutes
proposals.structural_mediator: Development of a uniform dispersion of fine Cu-rich, ductile second-phase particles embedded in the primary high-entropy matrix
proposals.mechanism: The ductile Cu-rich inclusions provide crack-tip shielding and enhance energy absorption under load, thereby arresting crack initiation and propagation, while the primary matrix retains its caloric phase transformation properties
proposals.predicted_outcome: Significantly increased toughness and ductility with improved load-bearing capacity, while the caloric performance under applied magnetic fields and pressures (within the original operational boundaries) remains essentially unchanged
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: This intervention leverages the composite concept—reinforcing a brittle matrix with a ductile phase in situ—to tailor the mechanical integrity without interfering with the mechanism of the caloric effects

proposals.intervention: Grain boundary engineering via controlled directional solidification and subsequent annealing
proposals.conditions: Perform directional solidification to align grains, followed by a post-solidification heat treatment at ≈700°C for 1 hour to promote the formation of high-angle, resilient grain boundaries
proposals.structural_mediator: Engineered grain boundary network with enhanced cohesion and reduced intergranular stress concentrations
proposals.mechanism: Aligned grains and optimized grain boundary character reduce the likelihood of intergranular cracking by distributing applied stresses more uniformly, while the bulk transformation responsible for the caloric effect is unaffected by these boundary modifications
proposals.predicted_outcome: Improved load-bearing performance with higher fracture toughness and resistance to cracking, and preservation of the caloric response (under the same magnetic and pressure-field conditions and temperature range as the base alloy)
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: The strategy specifically targets intergranular weaknesses—the primary crack initiation sites—by enhancing the grain boundary network, thereby increasing mechanical integrity while leaving the caloric phase transformation intact
